depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A person kneeling before a master 人 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 令 (lìng, command) — a person kneels before the master, waiting for the order. Kneeling to receive the word: a command.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'six': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 六 (liù, six) — picture the number six, counted out plainly. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Pieces 八 being further subdivided with a knife 刀  (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 分 (fēn, to divide) — a knife comes down between pieces that are spreading apart. The knife splitting them is the divide.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Walking 夂 and talking 口 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 各 (gè, individual) — a person comes walking in, speaking as they arrive. Each one arriving on their own: each, individual.

depicts: A big thick snake coiled up, its head raised at one end of the coil.
commentary: 巴 (bā) — the ancient picture is a big, thick snake coiled up with its head raised at one end. That coiled snake is what the strokes of 巴 still trace.

depicts: A cloud curling over on itself: a straight stroke on top with a spiral swirl hanging below.
commentary: 云 (yún, cloud) — A straight stroke sits on top while a spiral swirl curls below it. That curling swirl is the cloud taking shape.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A man 人 in a coffin; see 亾 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 亡 (wáng, death) — A figure lies enclosed in a coffin-like box. The hidden, enclosed body gives the sense of death and loss.

depicts: A person standing with legs crossed at the ankles and arms folded across the chest.
commentary: 交 (jiāo, to connect) — a person stands with legs crossed at the ankles and arms folded across the chest. Crossed limbs crossing over each other: to connect, to cross.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A man 儿 with two lines emphasizing their head 二 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 元 (yuán, first) — A person is drawn with two lines stressing the head at the top. The head is the first and chief part: 'first', 'primary'.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A stack of tablets (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 圭 (guī, jade tablet) — tablets are stacked one on another in a neat pile. The stacked tablets became this sign for the jade tablet.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: Grains of sand; 小 provides the pronunciation and meaning (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 少 (shǎo, few) — Only a few grains of sand are scattered in the picture. So little in view is the meaning: few, small in amount.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'especially': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 尤 (yóu, especially) — Picture one item singled out from the rest, marked as special. Use that singling-out as the cue for yóu, especially.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Simplified form of 開; hands 廾 lifting the latch 一 of a door (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 开 (kāi, to open) — two hands together lift the latch-bar of a door. Hands raising the bar: to open.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two trees 木 representing a forest (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 林 (lín, forest) — one tree stands beside another, 木 next to 木. Trees doubled are already a forest.

depicts: A kneeling woman shown by her two breasts, drawn as two dots inside her body's outline.
commentary: 母 (mǔ, mother) — A kneeling woman's outline, with two dots inside for breasts. Those two dots are the clue that this figure is a mother.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to begin': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 甫 (fǔ, to begin) — picture the first green sprout of something just starting to grow. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: To look someone in the eye 目 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 直 (zhí, straight) — An eye looks directly ahead, meeting another eye head-on. A gaze that does not bend or dodge is straight.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to depend on': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 乇 (tuō, to depend on) — Picture something leaning on or depending on a support. Use that reliance as the meaning cue for tuō.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'also': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 也 (yě, also) — Picture a plain link adding one thing to another: this, also. Use that adding-on sense as the cue for yě.

depicts: A tall gatehouse on a high mound: a roofed building raised on an earthen platform.
commentary: 京 (jīng, capital city) — a tall gatehouse stands raised on a high earthen mound. The lofty building on its platform is the capital's great gate.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Many people gathered 亼 under one roof (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 佥 (qiān, all) — Many people are gathered under a single roof. Everyone together in one place gives the sense of 'all'.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two hands 八 holding one object 廾 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 共 (gòng, all) — two hands together hold up one single object. Hands joined on one thing: shared by all.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A plate or flat dish; an everyday item (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 凡 (fán, any) — the picture is a plain plate, a flat everyday dish. The most ordinary thing there is stands for 'any, every'.

meaning: cutting off the feet as a form of punishment
depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'cutting off the feet as a form of punishment': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 刖 (yuè, cutting off the feet as a form of punishment) — Picture a plain punishment scene centred on the feet. Use it as a meaning cue for yuè.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Supporting a cause with the strength 力 of one's words 口 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 加 (jiā, to add to) — strength is lent to speech, force added behind the words. Adding on top: to add to.

depicts: An unborn baby curled up inside a womb that wraps around it like a bundle.
commentary: 包 (bāo, wrap) — a baby lies curled up inside the womb that wraps around it like a bundle. Something held snugly inside a wrapping: to wrap.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: To speak 口 omens ⺊ (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 占 (zhàn, to divine) — A mouth speaks out the omens shown by a sign above it. Reading and speaking the omen is divination.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A sprout growing in the ground, representing a budding talent (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 才 (cái, ability) — a sprout pushes up out of the ground. New growth just breaking through stands for a budding talent.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'daylight': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 旲 (tái, daylight) — Picture broad daylight, bright and open. Use the brightness as a plain meaning cue for tái.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Lumber 木 bound by rope 口 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 束 (shù, to bind) — Planks of wood are tied tightly together with rope around the middle. The rope doing the tying is the meaning: to bind.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'good': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 良 (liáng, good) — picture fine, clean grain poured out smooth and good. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'cannot': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 莫 (mò, cannot) — Picture a plain scene that says 'cannot', a blocked or refused action. Use the image as a meaning cue for mò.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'obstruction of breath (qi)': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 丂 (kǎo) — picture breath catching and blocked in the throat. A modern meaning picture for this old word for blocked breath, not an ancient form.

depicts: The green calyx of a flower: a small cup of pointed sepals on a stem that once held a bloom.
commentary: 不 (bù, no) — the drawing shows a flower's green calyx: a small cup of pointed sepals on a stem that once held a bloom. That little pointed cup is the picture behind the strokes.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A pregnant woman; compare 孕 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 乃 (nǎi, then) — The ancient form shows a pregnant woman, a curved body shape. Read that curved body as the core of the glyph.

depicts: A weaving shuttle: a pointed peg with thread being pushed across the warp threads.
commentary: 予 (yǔ, to give) — A weaving shuttle pushes thread across the warp, passing it from one side to the other. That passing-across is giving, handing over.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing '12th terrestrial branch': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 亥 (hài) — picture the twelfth and last marker in a cycle of twelve signs. A modern meaning picture for this calendar sign, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A plot of land 口 surrounded by a border 冂; 冂 also provides the pronunciation (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 冋 (jiōng, desert) — a plot of land lies inside an empty border, with nothing in it at all. Walled emptiness: open desert land.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to look upward': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 厃 (wěi, to look upward) — Picture a face turned up, looking upward. Use the upturned gaze as the meaning cue for wěi.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to go away': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 去 (qù, to go away) — Picture a figure leaving, moving away from where they were. Use the departure as the meaning cue for qù.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to spit out': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 咅 (pǒu, to spit out) — Picture the act of spitting something out, plain and direct. Use the mouth action as the meaning cue for pǒu.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'decisive': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 夬 (guài, decisive) — picture a clean, swift stroke that settles everything at once. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'head': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 头 (tóu, head) — Picture a head, drawn plainly and clearly. Use it as a direct meaning cue for tóu.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: An offering 土 in your hand 寸 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 寺 (sì, court) — A hand holds an offering at a formal place. The official, ceremonial setting gives the sense of a court.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing '5th heavenly stem': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 戊 (wù, 5th heavenly stem) — Picture a simple ordered marker for the fifth place in the heavenly-stem cycle. Use it as a meaning cue for wù, the 5th stem.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'small': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 戋 (jiān, small) — picture something tiny and slight, next to nothing. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'flat': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 扁 (biǎn, flat) — picture a board pressed flat and thin. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Twenty 廿 days ago 日 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 昔 (xī, past) — Many days, marked above a sun, have already gone by. Days behind the sun are days in the past.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'each': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 每 (měi, each) — picture items handed out one to every single person: each one gets one. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to fill': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 畐 (fú, to fill) — picture a vessel filled up completely full. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'according to': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 㠯 (yǐ, according to) — Picture a plain sign for following along with something, according to it. Use it as a meaning cue for yǐ.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to connect': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 丩 (jiū, to connect) — picture two lines winding together and joining into one. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A fist 九 holding a pebble 丶 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 丸 (wán, ball) — A fist closes around a small round pebble. The tiny round object in the hand is the ball or pellet.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'first time': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 乍 (zhà, first time) — Picture something happening suddenly, for the first time. Use that sudden first moment as the cue for zhà.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to study': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 习 (xí, to study) — Picture someone practising and reviewing, again and again. Use that repeated study as the meaning cue for xí.

depicts: The ground plan of a building drawn from above: a square outline with a cross-shaped inner plan.
commentary: 亚 (yà, Asia) — The drawing is a ground plan seen from above: a square outline with a cross-shaped inner plan. Read it as a map-like layout, flat and geometric.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A man standing with arrows pointing to his armpits (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 亦 (yì, also) — A standing figure has marks pointing to both armpits, picking out the sides of the body. Those side marks are the ancient indicator in this glyph.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: To hand 寸 something over to someone 亻  (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 付 (fù, give) — one person hands something over into another person's hand. Hand to hand: to give.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: Cracks in oracle bones used in fortune-telling (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 兆 (zhào, omen) — Cracks spread across a heated oracle bone, the pattern read for signs. Those cracks themselves are the omen.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A beast 兄 with two horns 丷 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 兑 (duì, cash) — a creature faces you with two horns spread above its head. Read the pair of spread horns at the top of the glyph.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'his': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 其 (qí, his) — Picture a plain pointer to possession, something belonging to him. Use it as a meaning cue for qí, 'his'.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A hand holding two sheafs of grain 禾 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 兼 (jiān, both) — one hand grips two sheaves of grain at the same time. Two held in a single grip: both.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: Simplified form of 岡, clouds 网 forming over a mountain 山 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 冈 (gāng, ridge or crest of hill) — clouds drift like a net over a mountain. The mountain's outline beneath the clouds is the ridge.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A container 凵 of wickedness 乂 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 凶 (xiōng, culprit) — A pit-like container holds a crossed, wicked mark inside it. Trouble trapped in the pit gives the sense of something ominous, a culprit.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to mow': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 刍 (chú, to mow) — picture a blade sweeping through tall grass, cutting it down. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to extend': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 及 (jí, to extend) — picture a hand reaching out, stretching to catch up and reach its goal. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two hands 又 joined, representing friendship; 又 also provides the pronunciation (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 友 (yǒu, friend) — Two hands reach toward each other and join. Hands joined in the same direction are friendship.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A hand 又 held up against a cliff 厂 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 反 (fǎn, reverse) — a hand presses up against a cliff face, pushing back against the rock. Pushing back: to reverse, to turn back.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A phrase 勹 from the mouth 口 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 句 (jù, sentence) — words come out of a mouth wrapped together as one phrase. A phrase out of the mouth: a sentence.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Simple words 八 coming from the mouth 口 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 只 (zhī, only) — Simple words come out of a mouth, nothing extra added. Just those words and no more: 'only'.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'imperial decree': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 召 (zhào, imperial decree) — Picture an official summons being issued, a decree calling someone in. Use that call as the meaning cue for zhào.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: One 一 voice 口 surrounded by conflict 戈 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 咸 (xián, all) — Weapons surround a single mouth giving one voice. One voice heard through the conflict gives the sense of 'all', together.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing '9th heavenly stem': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 壬 (rén, 9th heavenly stem) — Picture a simple ordered marker for the ninth place in the heavenly-stem cycle. Use it as a meaning cue for rén, the 9th stem.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A person with head tilted - leaning forward, running, energetic (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 夭 (yāo, young) — A young figure leans forward with head tilted, mid-run and full of energy. The lively, bending body shows youth.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A hand holding a large carpenter's square 工 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 巨 (jù, large) — a hand holds a big carpenter's square. The oversized measuring square stands for 'large'.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Simplified form of 並; two men standing side-by-side (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 并 (bìng, to combine) — the simpler written shape of 並: two figures stand side by side, brought together as one.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Bright and open, like the dawn 旦 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 昜 (yáng, bright) — The scene opens like dawn, light spreading wide and clear. That open brightness is the meaning to hold.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Variant of 何 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 曷 (hé, what) — this glyph is an old variant shape of 何, the question word. Read it as the same questioning figure that 何 carries.

depicts: A round fruit hanging at the very top of a tree, trunk and branches below it.
commentary: 果 (guǒ, fruit) — one round fruit hangs at the very top of the tree, trunk and branches below it. Fruit at the crown of the tree: the whole picture.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A foot 止 stopping in the right place 一 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 正 (zhèng, straight) — A foot comes to a stop exactly on the target line, in the right place. Stopping true and correct gives 'straight', 'upright'.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'this': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 此 (cǐ, this) — picture a finger pointing at the thing right here: this one. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A bolt of lightning zigzagging down from the sky.
commentary: 申 (shēn, to report) — A bolt of lightning zigzags down from the sky. That jagged bolt is the ancient shape preserved in the strokes.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to resemble': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 肖 (xiào, to resemble) — Picture two similar figures placed side by side so the likeness shows. Use that resemblance as the cue for xiào.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A bird settling into its nest, representing sunset; compare 東 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 覀 (xī, west) — The top part alone shows a bird settling into its nest at sunset. It carries the same sunset-and-west idea in a covering form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two people 从 together in a cart (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 两 (liǎng, two) — two people ride together in one cart, sharing the ride as a pair. Two together make the pair.

depicts: An oil lamp on a stand: a stem rising to a shallow dish with a single flame burning on top.
commentary: 主 (zhǔ, to own) — An oil lamp stands on its stem, a single flame burning in the dish on top. The flame is the main point of the lamp, the master point behind 'owner'.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to buy': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 买 (mǎi, to buy) — picture a hand paying out money and taking goods in exchange. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Simplified form of 爭, two hands 爪 and 彐 fighting over 亅 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 争 (zhēng, to dispute) — Two hands pull and fight over the same small object between them. Two sides grabbing at one thing is a dispute.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to take small steps': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 亍 (chù, to take small steps) — picture short, careful little steps taken one after another. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Five elements (the cross with the extra stroke) between heaven 一 and earth 一  (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 五 (wǔ, five) — A crossed sign sits between a line of heaven above and a line of earth below. The old fivefold scheme is packed into that small crossed mark.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A mouth 亼 talking about things (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 今 (jīn, now) — a mouth speaks about the things of the present moment. Speech about right now: now, the present day.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A border 八 dividing people 人 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 介 (jiè, agent) — a person stands on the border line that divides one side from another. Standing on the dividing line: the go-between, the agent.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Simplified form of 倉; grains 食 kept in storage 口 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 仓 (cāng, granary) — grain is heaped up and kept stored inside a storehouse. Grain kept safe under a cover: a granary.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'surplus': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 余 (yú, surplus) — Picture more than enough left over after the main amount is taken. Use the leftover as the cue for yú, surplus.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to consent': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 俞 (yú, to consent) — Picture a person nodding in agreement, saying yes. Use that nod of consent as the meaning cue for yú.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Someone stepping 止 in front of another person 儿 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 先 (xiān, first) — One figure steps ahead, in front of another person. Being out in front is being first.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A man 人  entering a door 冂 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 内 (nèi, inside) — A person steps through a doorway frame. Follow the figure inward: crossing the frame means going inside.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Soldiers 冖 (distorted 力) in a cart 车 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 军 (jūn, army) — soldiers are packed into a war cart under its cover. Troops carried in the cart: an army.

depicts: A length of thread with a knot tied at both ends, hanging down.
commentary: 冬 (dōng, winter) — a length of thread hangs with a knot tied at each end, finished and put away. Thread tied off and done: the picture behind 'winter'.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'a line': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 列 (liè, a line) — picture things set out in a row, one after another. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Laws inscribed 刂 on a slate 贝 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 则 (zé, rule) — Laws are cut into a solid slate with a blade, fixed for everyone to follow. Rules carved in stone are rules indeed.

depicts: A ladle: a small round cup with a long handle curving out of it.
commentary: 勺 (sháo, spoon) — A small round ladle cup curves into a long handle. The cup-and-handle shape maps straight onto the glyph.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to hook': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 勾 (gōu, to hook) — picture a curved hook catching hold and holding fast. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to change': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 化 (huà, to change) — picture one thing turning into something else entirely. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: Two people 匕 sitting back-to-back; phonetic loan for "north" (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 北 (běi, north) — two people sit back to back. The picture of backs was borrowed for its sound to write 'north'.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Ten 十 different types of grass 艹 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 卉 (huì, general term for plants) — grasses of many kinds stand together in one bunch. Ten kinds of grass at once: plants in general.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A cow 牛 splitting 丷 wood in half (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 半 (bàn, half) — a cow stands by as wood is split down the middle. The split makes two equal parts: a half.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A hand 又(altered) holding an empty shell 甲 (altered) (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 卑 (bēi, humble) — a hand holds out an empty shell, offering nothing of any worth. Empty-handed and lowly: humble.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing '4th terrestrial branch': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 卯 (mǎo) — picture the fourth marker in a cycle of twelve signs. A modern meaning picture for this calendar sign, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to issue': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 发 (fā, to issue) — picture something being sent forth and let go, issued out. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A hand 又 taking the ear 耳 of a fallen enemy (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 取 (qǔ, to take) — A hand reaches in and takes an ear. The grabbing hand is the action to read: to take.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'platform': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 台 (tái, platform) — Picture a raised flat platform you can stand or place things on. Use the raised surface as the meaning cue for tái.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: To speak 口 with the force of an ox 牛 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 告 (gào, to tell) — an ox stands behind a mouth: speech with an ox's force behind it. Forceful speech: to tell, to announce.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A drum 口 on a stand with feathers 土 on top (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 壴 (zhù, drum) — A drum sits mounted on a stand, with feather decorations on top. The mounted drum, dressed for ceremony, is the whole picture.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'central': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 央 (yāng, central) — Picture the exact centre point, with everything arranged around it. Use that middle position as the cue for yāng, central.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A person 大 riding a horse 可 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 奇 (qí, strange) — A big person appears to ride an unlikely mount in the ancient compound. The odd, unbalanced scene itself signals 'strange'.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to announce': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 尃 (fū, to announce) — picture a herald calling out news for everyone to hear. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'you': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 尔 (ěr, you) — picture one person singled out and pointed to: you. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'a legendary ancient emperor-sage': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 尧 (yáo, a legendary emperor-sage) — Picture a revered emperor-sage figure standing in dignified form. Use the figure as a name cue for yáo.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'village': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 屯 (tún, village) — Picture a small settled village, a cluster of dwellings together. Use the settlement as the meaning cue for tún.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'young brother': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 弟 (dì, young brother) — picture a young boy, the little brother of the family. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to accomplish': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 成 (chéng, to accomplish) — picture a task brought through to completion, finished and done. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: The first rays 十 of the sun 日 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 早 (zǎo, early) — The sun has just risen, its first rays marked above it. Sunrise itself is early morning.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two hands 日, 又 pulling an eye open 罒 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 曼 (màn, long) — two hands stretch an eye wide open, pulling it long. Stretched out wide gives the sense of long, extended.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A wheat plant that has not yet borne fruit; compare 來 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 未 (wèi, not yet) — A young wheat plant stands full of growth but with no fruit yet. Grown, but not yet ripe: that timing is the meaning.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: The sweet 甘 fruit of a certain tree 木 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 某 (mǒu, some) — Look for sweet fruit hanging on one particular tree. One specific, unnamed tree gives the sense of 'some' or 'a certain'.

meaning: the name of an ancient tribe
depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'the name of an ancient tribe': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 氐 (dī) — picture the camp of an old tribe settled on the lowland. A modern meaning picture for this tribe's name, not an ancient form.

depicts: Water gushing out of a round spring mouth in rock and streaming away below it.
commentary: 泉 (quán, spring) — Water bursts from a round spring mouth in rock and streams away below it. The source in the rock is what makes it a spring, not a river.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to lead on to': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 爰 (yuán, to lead on to) — Picture one thing leading onward to the next in sequence. Use that leading-on movement as the cue for yuán.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'path': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 甬 (yǒng, path) — Picture a clear path leading forward. Use the path itself as the meaning cue for yǒng.

depicts: A bird settled in its nest at sunset: a round nest with a bird resting inside it.
commentary: 西 (xī, west) — A bird settles into its round nest as the sun sets. Birds roosting at sunset point to the west, where the sun goes down.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A feathered crown (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 酋 (qiú, chief of a tribe) — A feathered crown fills the picture. The headdress marks the wearer as a chief.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A hand picking 爫 fruit from a tree 木 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 采 (cǎi, to collect) — a hand reaches into a tree and picks the fruit. Hand plus tree: gathering in.

meaning: Form of 卷 used as a phonetic component
depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'Form of 卷 used as a phonetic component': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 龹 (quǎn, form of 卷 used as a phonetic component) — Picture this as a plain form cue for the 卷-related component. Use it as a meaning picture for quǎn.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'pennant': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 㐬 (liú, pennant) — picture a long pennant streaming in the wind from its pole. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A foot 止 strolling down the road 廴 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 㢟 (chān, to walk slowly) — a foot strolls unhurried down a long road. The road stretches out under the foot: a slow walk.

depicts: A scorpion: a round body with claws at the front, jointed legs at the sides and a curved sting tail.
commentary: 万 (wàn, ten thousand) — A scorpion: a round body, front claws, jointed legs and a curved sting tail. That creature is the ancient shape behind this number word.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'concentrated': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 专 (zhuān, concentrated) — Picture attention focused on one single point, nothing else. Use that single focus as the cue for zhuān, concentrated.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: Two hills (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 丘 (qiū, mound) — Two low hills rise side by side. Their rounded humps are exactly the mound shape in the glyph.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two people sitting side-by-side; compare 竝 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 並 (bìng, to combine) — two people sit side by side in a row. Two brought together in one row: combined.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'right conduct': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 义 (yì, right conduct) — Picture a person doing the right thing, plainly and uprightly. Use that upright conduct as the cue for yì.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A person 夭 on stilts (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 乔 (qiáo, tall) — A person stands raised up on stilts. The extra height in the picture is the whole point: tall.

depicts: The square wooden frame of a well seen from above: crossed timbers forming a grid over the opening.
commentary: 井 (jǐng, well) — seen from above, crossed timbers make a square frame over the well's mouth. That grid of the well frame is the whole glyph.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'high': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 亢 (kàng, high) — picture a head held high, the neck stretched up tall. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A tree 木 bearing fruit 立 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 亲 (qīn, relatives) — A tree puts out new growth above it, like one generation rising from another. That family-tree image links the parts to kin and relatives.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Old variant of 冰 ("ice-water") (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 仌 (bīng, frozen) — this is the old variant of 冰: drops of water stiffened into ice. Frozen water is the whole picture.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'logical reasons': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 仑 (lún, logical reasons) — picture thoughts lined up in order, reasoned through step by step. A modern meaning picture for 'logical order', not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A man 亻 caught 弋 by the passing of time (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 代 (dài, era) — a man is caught as time sweeps past him. One person gives way to the next as the years pass: an era, a generation.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: One hundred 百 people 亻; 百 also provides the pronunciation (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 佰 (bǎi, hundred) — a person stands beside 百, one hundred, and the 百 also supplies the sound bǎi. A person reckoning in hundreds.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to grant': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 允 (yǔn, to grant) — Picture someone giving permission, granting a request with a nod. Use that granting gesture as the cue for yǔn.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A person 儿 carrying a torch 火 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 光 (guāng, light) — a person carries a burning torch held high. The flame borne above the person is the light.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to spare': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two hands 八 holding an axe 丘 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 兵 (bīng, soldier) — two hands grip an axe and hold it up together. Hands on a weapon: a soldier.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to risk': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 冒 (mào, to risk) — picture someone plunging headfirst into danger. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: Simplified form of 農, tilling the field 田 with a hoe 辰 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 农 (nóng, agriculture) — The scene is farm work: a field being tilled with a hoe. Tools plus field give you agriculture.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A sprout 屮 growing out of a container 凵 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 出 (chū, to go out) — a sprout grows up and out of an open container. Breaking out of the container: to go out.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Simplified form of 擊; 手 provides the meaning (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 击 (jī, to strike) — in the fuller old form 擊, a hand does the hitting. The hand is the meaning: to strike.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to cut': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 切 (qiè, to cut) — Picture a blade cutting cleanly through something. Use the cutting action as a direct meaning cue for qiè.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Harvesting 刂 grain 禾 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 利 (lì, gains) — a knife blade cuts through ripe grain at harvest time. Cutting in the harvest: the gains.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to go to': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 到 (dào, to go to) — picture a traveler arriving and stepping up to the destination. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A roll of cloth (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 匹 (pǐ, bolt of cloth) — A neat roll of cloth fills the picture. The rolled length is the measure: one bolt.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'noon': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 午 (wǔ, noon) — Picture the sun at its highest, at midday. Use that peak-of-the-day moment as the cue for wǔ, noon.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'single': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 单 (dān, single) — picture one single thing standing all by itself, alone. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A musical bell (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 南 (nán, south) — The ancient form is a hanging musical bell. The bell shape, not a compass point, is what the strokes preserve.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'still': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 却 (què, still) — Picture a calm, still scene with movement held back. Use that held-back feeling as the cue for què.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A curled up scroll 㔾 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 卷 (juǎn, book) — a scroll curls up on itself into a roll. The curled scroll is the old form of a book.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'whetstone': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 厉 (lì, whetstone) — picture a blade being ground back and forth on a rough stone. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'county': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 县 (xiàn, county) — Picture a county town or district in a plain scene. Use it as a meaning cue for xiàn, a county.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to take part in': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 参 (cān, to take part in) — picture people joining in together on one shared task. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two hands 又 side-by-side (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 双 (shuāng, pair) — Two hands sit side by side, matching each other. Two of a kind together make a pair.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: The smaller 小 brother (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 叔 (shū, uncle) — The ancient compound points to the smaller, younger brother. A younger brother of a parent is an uncle.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Something 冖 passed from one hand 爫 to another 又 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 受 (shòu, to receive) — Under a cover, something is passed from one hand into another. One hand gives and the other receives: watch the transfer.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A hand 乂 using a pen to record a history (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 史 (shǐ, history) — A hand holds a pen over a record, writing events down. The recording hand is the scribe, and the scribe makes history.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A person speaking orders 口 and raising their arm (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 司 (sī, to take charge of) — A figure raises an arm and gives orders through an open mouth. That commanding pose is managing, taking charge.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: One with wooden 木 speech 口 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 呆 (dāi, dull) — a mouth set over wood: speech as stiff and blank as a block of wood. Wooden speech: dull.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: One person talking 可 over another 可 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 哥 (gē, elder brother) — two mouths are stacked one above the other, the upper one speaking over the lower. The one on top, speaking first: the elder brother.

depicts: A whirlpool: two concentric squared spirals turning around a centre.
commentary: 回 (huí, to return) — a whirlpool: two squared spirals turn around one center. Water circling back on itself: to return, to turn back.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'cause': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 因 (yīn, cause) — Picture a plain scene where one thing is the reason for another. Use that reason-link as the meaning cue for yīn.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Simplified form of 聖; a king 王 of listening 耳  and speaking口 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 圣 (shèng, holy) — The simplified form joins an ear, a mouth and a kingly figure below. Listening and speaking with authority give the sage-like, holy figure.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two people 从 sitting on the ground 土 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 坐 (zuò, seat) — Two people sit facing each other on the ground itself. Their seated posture on the earth is exactly the action: to sit.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'big': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 壮 (zhuàng, big) — Picture a robust, strongly built figure, big and sturdy. Use that sturdy size as the cue for zhuàng.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A person 亻 sneaking by under cover 亠 of night 夕 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 夜 (yè, night) — A person moves quietly under a cover, with an evening sign beside them. Movement hidden by darkness is night.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A giant 大 with a normal-sized man 丶 for scale (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 太 (tài, very) — A giant figure towers in the picture, with a tiny dot beside it for scale. Bigger than the ordinary big figure itself: 'very', 'too much'.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to offer': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 奉 (fèng, to offer) — picture both hands lifting a gift up to present it. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to appoint': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 委 (wěi, to appoint) — Picture one person handing a charge to another, an appointment being made. Use that handover as the cue for wěi.

depicts: A snake with its head raised: a small head and a very long body curving down into a drooping tail.
commentary: 它 (tā, it) — A snake raises its small head, its long body curving down into a drooping tail. The snake shape is the ancient core behind this pronoun.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to complete': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 完 (wán, to complete) — Picture a finished task, complete with nothing left over. Use that finished state as the meaning cue for wán.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A memorial service 且 held in a house 宀 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 宜 (yí, fitting) — Inside a house, a memorial offering is set out in its proper place. Everything in its right place is what is fitting and appropriate.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A person 各 welcomed under one's roof 宀; 各 also provides the pronunciation (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 客 (kè, guest) — a visitor arrives and is welcomed in under the roof, and 各 also lends the sound kè. A person received under your roof: a guest.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A person 亻 sleeping in a bed 百 under a roof 宀 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 宿 (sù, to stop) — Under a roof, a person lies down in a bed to sleep. Roof plus sleeper means lodging and stopping for the night.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to examine': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 察 (chá, to examine) — picture an eye looking closely, inspecting something piece by piece. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A pair 又 of hands 寸 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 对 (duì, correct) — two hands are set facing each other, matched as a pair. Matched up evenly: correct, facing.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A bow 身 being drawn by a hand 寸 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 射 (shè, to shoot) — A bow is pulled back by a hand, ready to loose an arrow. The drawn bow is the shooting action frozen in the glyph.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to taste': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 尝 (cháng, to taste) — picture a tongue taking a first small lick to test the flavor. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Picture of a man measuring by pacing (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 尺 (chǐ, ruler) — a man measures out distance by pacing it, step by step. Pacing out lengths gives the measuring unit, the ruler.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: To stop 至 under a roof 尸 (variant of 厂) (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 屋 (wū, building) — A figure comes to rest under a roofed structure. Roof plus stopping place gives a building, a house.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'village': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 庄 (zhuāng, village) — Picture a small village settlement, houses clustered together. Use the settlement as the meaning cue for zhuāng.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A stable 广 where carriages 车 are parked (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 库 (kù, armory) — carriages are parked in rows inside a storehouse shed. War gear kept under cover: the armory.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Twenty 廿 people 又 meeting inside a building 广 to deliberate (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 度 (dù, degree) — people gather under a roof, hands at work measuring and deliberating together. Measuring things out gives 'degree', a measured amount.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A foot on the road 㢟 stopped in its tracks 丿 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 延 (yán, to defer) — A foot on the road is stopped in its tracks, held up mid-journey. Being held up and stretched out in time is 'to defer', to extend.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A craftsman using an awl 弋 and a measuring square 工 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 式 (shì, formula) — A craftsman works with an awl beside a measuring square. Measured, standard work gives the sense of a set formula or style.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to display': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 张 (zhāng, to display) — Picture something opened out and put on display, spread wide. Use that spreading-open as the cue for zhāng.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Like 亦 a bow 弓 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 弯 (wān, bend) — The shape curves like a drawn bow. Follow the curve: to bend is to curve out of straight.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A brush used to record stories (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 录 (lù, to copy) — the picture is a brush, the tool for writing stories down. The recording brush is the whole sign.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A decisive 夬 will 忄; 夬 also provides the pronunciation (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 快 (kuài, speedy) — a decisive heart acts without delay, the will made up in an instant — and 夬 lends the sound kuài. A quick decision in the heart: speedy.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Many mouths 口 speaking with one mind 心 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 总 (zǒng, to gather) — Many mouths speak together, gathered under one shared mind and heart. Everything brought into one is 'to gather', 'total'.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two hearts 心 beating together 咸 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 感 (gǎn, to affect) — two hearts beat together as one. Hearts moving each other: to feel, to affect.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A hand 扌 holding a weapon 戈 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 我 (wǒ, I) — A hand grips a halberd weapon, ready and armed. The armed self standing its ground becomes the word for 'I'.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Two hands 廾 brandishing a spear 戈 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 戒 (jiè, to warn) — two hands grip a spear and hold it up in warning. A weapon raised by both hands: stand warned.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: To defend yourself 口 with a spear 戈; "or else" (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 或 (huò, or) — a spear is held ready to defend what is yours: hold your ground, or else. The guarded choice gives 'or'.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to pull': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 拉 (lā, to pull) — picture a hand dragging something along behind it. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'in charge': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 掌 (zhǎng, in charge) — Picture an open palm held up in control, in charge of the situation. Use the palm as the meaning cue for zhǎng.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'reason': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 故 (gù, reason) — picture the old cause behind a thing: the reason why. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'fast': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 敏 (mǐn, fast) — picture quick hands at work, swift and sharp. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to respect': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 敬 (jìng, to respect) — picture a deep, respectful bow made before an elder. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A freshly chopped 斤 tree 亲 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 新 (xīn, new) — An axe has just cut into a tree, leaving a fresh surface. Freshly cut wood is new wood: that is the link.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A person 旡 turning away from food 皀; compare 即 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 既 (jì, already) — a person turns away from the food dish: the meal is finished. Turning from a finished meal: already done.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: The light of the sun 日 and moon 月 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 明 (míng, bright) — Sun on one side and moon on the other, both giving light. Put the two brightest things in the sky together and you get brightness.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Th sun 日 setting behind a village 氏 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 昏 (hūn, dusk) — the sun sinks low behind the village. Sun going down on the settlement: dusk.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to change': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 易 (yì, to change) — Picture one thing changing into another, a clear before-and-after. Use that transformation as the cue for yì.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'star': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 星 (xīng, star) — Picture a bright star in a night sky, drawn plainly. Use the star itself as the meaning cue for xīng.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: The sun 日 rising over a city 京; 京 also provides the pronunciation (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 景 (jǐng, scenery) — the sun rises over the capital's gatehouse, and 京 also lends the sound jǐng. Sunlight over the city: the view, the scenery.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A man with head 日 and hands 共 tormenting a deer 水 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 暴 (bào, violent) — the old compound shows hands laying into a creature with force. That rough handling is the picture of violence.

depicts: A shallow rectangular tray with bent-up sides — a frame used for raising silkworms.
commentary: 曲 (qū, crooked) — A shallow tray has its sides bent upward, a frame for raising silkworms. Notice the bent edges: nothing here is straight, hence 'crooked'.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: One man 夫 replacing another; 日 provides the pronunciation (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 替 (tì, to change) — One figure steps in as another steps out, taking his place. The swap itself is the meaning: to replace, to change.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to have': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 有 (yǒu, to have) — Picture someone with something in their possession, plain and clear. Use that having as the meaning cue for yǒu.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to face': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 朝 (cháo, to face) — picture a courtier turning to face the rising sun at morning court. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: The top 一 of a tree 木 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 末 (mò, end) — The same tree as in 本, but notice the top: the highest twig is picked out in gold. The gold mark points to the tip, the end of the tree.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Flowers 几 blooming on a tree 木 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 朵 (duǒ, cluster of flowers) — blossoms bloom out from the top of a tree. A bunch of flowers on the wood: a cluster.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A hand using a chisel 殳 to cut stone (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 段 (duàn, section) — a hand drives a chisel into stone and cuts a piece free. A piece cut off is a section.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: An eye 巳 pierced by a dagger 戈, an old mark of slavery (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 民 (mín, citizens) — an eye pierced by a dagger: a harsh old mark for slaves. That mark came to name the common people, the citizens.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'long': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 永 (yǒng, long) — Picture something stretching out long and unending into the distance. Use its length as the meaning cue for yǒng.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'waves': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 波 (bō, waves) — picture waves rolling across the water one after another. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to exist': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 活 (huó, to exist) — picture something breathing and moving, full of life. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: The remains of a fire 火; 火 also provides the pronunciation (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 灰 (huī, ashes) — the grey remains left where a fire has burned out. Ashes are what the fire leaves behind — and 火 fire also lends the sound.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'certainly': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 然 (rán, certainly) — Picture a clear 'yes, that is so' moment, plain and certain. Use it as a meaning cue for rán.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'insane': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 狂 (kuáng, insane) — picture a wild dog raging completely out of control. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A string 幺 vibrating in an instrument 亠十 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 率 (lǜ, to command) — a string stretched on an instrument vibrates as it sounds. That taut, sounding string is the picture at the center.

depicts: A broad shield with one eye peeking over its top edge.
commentary: 盾 (dùn, shield) — a broad shield fills the picture, with one eye peeking over its top edge. The eye watching above the shield is still in the glyph.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to know': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 知 (zhī, to know) — Picture a clear moment of knowing, an answer falling into place. Use it as a plain meaning cue for zhī.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Flames 覀 over an altar 示, referring to a Chinese tradition of burning fake money as an offering (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 票 (piào, bank note) — Flames rise over an altar where paper money is burned as an offering. The paper in the flames is the link to a note.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: An animal standing straight; 亠 is the head (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 离 (lí, rare beast) — an animal stands upright in the picture, its head at the very top. That standing beast is the ancient form.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'elegant': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 秀 (xiù, elegant) — Picture a fine, elegant figure standing out gracefully. Use that grace as the meaning cue for xiù.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: The time of year when farmers would burn 禾 crops 火 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 秋 (qiū, autumn) — Grain stands beside fire, recalling fields burned after harvest. Harvest time plus fire gives you autumn.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'hollow': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 空 (kōng, hollow) — picture an empty cave with nothing inside it at all. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: The ten 十 movements of a piece of music 音 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 章 (zhāng, chapter) — The ancient compound links a piece of music with its complete set of movements. A finished movement is a section, a chapter.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A child standing 立 in the village 里 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 童 (tóng, child) — A young figure stands upright in a village setting. The small standing figure is the child.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'treaty': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 约 (yuē, treaty) — Picture two sides bound by an agreement, a treaty being sealed. Use that binding agreement as the cue for yuē.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Stuck in a net 罒, unable to leave 去 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 罢 (bà, to cease) — a creature is caught in a net and cannot get away to leave. Trapped and stopped, with no way onward: to cease.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'to test': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 考 (kǎo, to test) — picture an elder being questioned, his answers put to the test. A modern meaning picture, not an ancient form.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: A pregnant woman with a baby ⺼ in her womb (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 育 (yù, to produce) — A pregnant woman carries a child in her womb, shown as flesh enclosing new life. Bringing forth life is to produce, to raise.

depicts: A stomach: a curved sac filled with grain, sitting above a strip of flesh.
commentary: 胃 (wèi, stomach) — A curved stomach sac sits filled with grain above a strip of flesh. The food-holding sac is the stomach.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient pictographic form: A bear's head 厶, body ⺼, and claws 匕 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 能 (néng, can) — In the ancient form, pick out a bear's head, body and claws. The strong animal stands behind the sense of ability.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'house': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 舍 (shě, house) — Picture a simple house or lodging, drawn plainly. Use the building as a direct meaning cue for shě.

depicts: Drawn from the ancient compound (ideographic) form: Using a tool 殳 to sort items on a tray 舟 (shown as the scene itself, plainly drawn).
commentary: 般 (bān, sort) — hands work over a tray with a tool, sorting the items on it into kinds. Sorting into kinds is the whole meaning.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'if': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 若 (ruò, if) — Picture a fork in the path, as if asking what happens if you go one way. Use that open choice as the cue for ruò, 'if'.

depicts: A plain modern picture representing 'although': the clearest everyday object or scene for this meaning, drawn simply.
commentary: 虽 (suī, although) — Picture a turn in the road, where the scene continues although something blocks it. Use that contrast as the cue for suī, 'although'.

depicts: A person standing with both hands planted on their waist, elbows out.
commentary: 要 (yào, essential) — A person stands firm with both hands planted on their waist, elbows out. That planted stance at the body's middle gives the waist, and what is essential and wanted.
